article_title: Mind the Gap: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary
citation: Dorsett, R., Rienzo, C., Rolfe, H., Burns, H., Robertson, B.-A., Thorpe, B., & Wall, K. (2014). Mind the Gap: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary. Education Endowment Foundation. https://www.educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk
title: The 5Rs learning dispositions framework: Readiness, Resourcefulness, Resilience, Responsibility and Reflectiveness
description: The 5Rs is "a learning dispositions framewor k" developed by the Campaign for Learning, comprising "Readiness, Resourcefulness, Resilience, Responsibility and Reflectiveness". In Mind the Gap it structures the animation course: each session of the five-session programme was matched to one of the 5Rs, so that session 1 focused on Readiness, session 2 on Resourcefulness, session 3 on Responsibility, session 4 on Resilience and session 5 on Reflection. The progression through the programme was mapped so that metacognitive elements and the animation process were closely associated, maximising opportunities for transfer.
requirements: Facilitators use standardised resources (a session presentation, a family handbook and a teachers' handbook) so the same focus on metacognition is maintained across schools
constraints: The framework is applied within a family learning setting where children and parents work together; the report does not claim effects for the framework itself separately from the course
examples: Session 1 (Readiness) included an introduction to metacognition and using modelling clay to consider 'what kind of learner am I?'; session 5 (Reflection) involved finishing films, sharing them, and reflecting on what had been learned
